column1: # Text fields are stored and returned verbatim as application/json; the web and mobile clients
# escape on render (no innerHTML or bypassSecurityTrust* in the Angular app, React Native Text),
# and the server renders no HTML. ZAP raises this variant at Low risk / Low confidence only
# because its payload came back in a JSON body. Scoped to the JSON API, not ignored globally.
# Check 6-5 (Low confidence, no evidence) infers path traversal when a made-up name is rejected
# and the URL's own last segment ("catalog", "barbers", an id) is accepted. Creating or renaming a
# record whose name must be unique behaves exactly like that: ZAP's fixed made-up name is a
# duplicate (409) after its first use, the next unused name succeeds. Which of these endpoints it
# lands on varies from run to run. The names are database values, never paths.
